classification.difficultyReason: Adjust the available people and places for fixed membership, then combine the already counted disjoint cases for the restriction against including both people.

content.prompt: A committee of 6 is to be chosen from 14 people, including Bob and Mary. How many committees can be formed if

children.label: a
children.prompt: Bob and Mary must both be on the committee.

answer.worked:
Bob and Mary fill two places. Choose the remaining four members from the other 12 people.
$$N=\binom{12}{4}=495.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: neither Bob nor Mary are on the committee.

answer.worked:
Exclude Bob and Mary, then choose all six members from the remaining 12 people.
$$N=\binom{12}{6}=924.$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: exactly one of Bob or Mary is on the committee.

answer.worked:
Choose which of Bob and Mary is included, then choose five members from the other 12 people.
$$N=2\binom{12}{5}=1584.$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Bob and Mary are not allowed to both be on the committee.

answer.short:
$\binom{12}{6}+2\binom{12}{5}=2508$

Add the cases with neither included and exactly one included.
answer.worked:
The allowed cases are neither Bob nor Mary, or exactly one of them. These cases are disjoint.
$$\begin{align*}N&=\binom{12}{6}+2\binom{12}{5}\\N&=924+1584\\N&=2508.\end{align*}$$
